summary: IntervalSpec uses fixed UTC second alignment and ignores ScheduleSpec.timezone for day-sized intervals, causing scheduled workflows to drift during DST transitions. The team agreed to implement RRULE (RFC 5545) support in ScheduleSpec for calendar-style recurrence rather than modifying IntervalSpec semantics.
userImpact: Users with DST-aware timezones using day-sized intervals experience scheduling drift when DST transitions occur, causing workflows to run at different UTC times than expected.
rootCause: IntervalSpec uses fixed UTC second alignment and doesn't account for timezone-based calendar days; StructuredCalendar/cron paths properly use time.Location but interval-only schedules do not.
proposedFix: Add calendar-style recurrence via ScheduleSpec.rrule field (RFC 5545 line bodies) with a practical subset (FREQ/INTERVAL with DTSTART + timezone/TZID semantics), keeping IntervalSpec as simple epoch + phase semantics.
workaround: Use StructuredCalendar or cron-style specs which already respect timezone, or map 'every N local days' to calendar/cron specs instead of Interval.
keyQuote: RRULE (RFC 5545) in the spirit of the thread—with a **practical subset** to start (e.g. `FREQ`/`INTERVAL` with `DTSTART` + `timezone` / `TZID` semantics) rather than entangling that behavior into `IntervalSpec`.
